name: Jamaica Inn
positioning: Family-run British colonial-style inn on an eight-acre property with a secluded crescent beach in Ocho Rios
best_for: Couples who want a cottage or suite steps from a secluded beach
Travelers who want to switch off, with no TVs or radios

facts.text: Jamaica Inn sits on an eight-acre property with a secluded beach.
The beach is a 700-foot stretch of golden shore.
The British colonial-style inn has no TVs or radios.
The hotel's look features white columns and blue arches.
The Morrow family has run the hotel since 1958.
All stays include resort amenities, continental breakfast, afternoon tea and evening hors d'oeuvres.
The one-bedroom cottages each have an elegant living and bar space, an infinity plunge pool, ocean views and private sea access.
The Cowdray Suite is a large first-floor suite with a separate dressing room, a large balcony veranda and sunset views of the sea and mountains.
The Beach Wing suites have antique furniture and fresh flowers inside.
The hotel is a member of the White River Foundation and takes part in a coral restoration programme.
Every Saturday the hotel offers complimentary croquet tuition with a glass of rose.
The Terrace restaurant serves an ever-changing menu of island ingredients with live music each evening.

highlights.text: Suite 21, the largest suite, sits on a secluded peninsula with its own private grounds, an oceanfront sundeck and a plunge pool.
The hotel's crescent-shaped secluded beach is a stretch of golden sand.
The cottages have Indonesian-style interiors, private plunge pools and secluded outdoor showers.
The Ocean Spa is an oceanfront spa with a saltwater sea bath.
The hotel has had resident black Labradors since the 1970s, and Shadow V has her own cottage on the property.

considerations.text: Jamaica Inn is about an hour and a half from the airports in Montego Bay and Kingston.
WhataHotel notes limited modern amenities and technology.
